extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, engineers, and educated general readers interested in physics/engineering/industrial physiology
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative guidance for assessing multi-author scientific volumes, individual technical articles, experimental/observational reports, and studies of industrial/physiological efficiency as exemplified by book reviews and current-topic reports in a scientific journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness / wealth of material
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘the unexampled wealth of material’ — coverage across many topics (mechanics, engineering, heat) and numerous articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use breadth as a positive feature but recognise that a treatise planned on a comprehensive scale will inevitably have sins of omission; reviewer’s role includes pointing out such omissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authoritativeness, maturity of judgment, originality and freshness
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘the authoritativeness, the maturity of judgment, the originality and inviting freshness of treatment which are exhibited by the majority of the writers’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate contributions for authoritative voice, mature judgement, and original, fresh treatment of topics rather than mere compilation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate choice of contributors (accepted authorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: A glance at the names of contributors furnishes sufficient guarantee that the various subjects are dealt with by accepted authorities and experienced investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that subjects are handled by recognised experts; contributor credentials strengthen a volume's reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duty to identify omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘probably the only useful service that a reviewer can hope to perform is to point out a few of the sins of omission which are inevitable’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even for thorough volumes, explicitly note missing topics or perspectives that readers might expect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate balance between textbook exposition and research methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation that methods employed by research workers differ from those described in text-books (example: calorimetry articles showing modern research methods vs textbook methods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether an article appropriately reflects current research practice versus repeating textbook approaches; prefer up-to-date methods and demonstrations of practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of experimental/model results to full-scale machines
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The results of wind-channel and ship-tank experiments on models can be applied to full-scale machines by the use of the Principle of Similitude’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether model/scale experiments are correctly connected to full-scale applications (use of similitude/principle of similitude).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of future trends and outlook
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism for omission: ‘one would have liked to know something of the writers’ views on the future trend of their subjects’ (example: possibilities of the gas turbine or steam turbine for aircraft/locomotives).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valuable article or chapter should state the author’s view of future directions, potential developments, and unresolved practical challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness with respect to present-day practice
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘These articles cover the ground pretty thoroughly, so far as present-day practice goes.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the treatment is adequate for current practice and technologies; distinguish exhaustive contemporary surveys from historical or elementary accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and discussion of practical applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Noting omission of important practical applications (e.g., airship and aeroplane structures in a strength-of-structures article; gyroscopes lacking mention of gyro-compasses, stabilisers, aeroplane-level indicators).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether theoretical or brief articles sufficiently address practical/industrial applications and modern uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate organization and topical placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique that certain subjects are awkwardly housed (e.g., elementary thermoelectric pyrometer account within elasticity article; permeability of concrete and attrition tests in elastic constants article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether topics are grouped and located appropriately within the work; misplaced sections reduce coherence and reader utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and relevance of illustrations and figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: Fig. 120 transferred direct from a catalogue ‘without the superfluous lettering being removed’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that illustrations are clear, properly edited for publication (no catalogue artefacts), and genuinely support the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of depth and length across articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrast between a brief theoretical article (11 pages) and a much longer testing-focused article (125 pages) — desire for inclusion of mathematical researches in the shorter piece and more exhaustive treatment of some topics in the longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether article length matches the subject's complexity and whether complementary articles provide the expected depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on modern measurement methods (electrical methods prominence)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Electrical methods of calorimetry naturally occupy a prominent place, for the ease with which electrical energy can be measured and controlled has placed a powerful tool in the hands of workers concerned with thermal measurements.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value prominence given to measurement techniques that offer improved control/accuracy; ensure modern methods are adequately explained and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of detailed calibration procedures and precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed descriptions of methods for calibration and ‘the precautions which must be observed’ for platinum resistance thermometers calibrated at ice, steam, and sulphur points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement-focused articles should give clear, reproducible calibration procedures and note necessary precautions for accurate results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical underpinning of instrument design and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable discussion of theory underlying use of red glass for approximately monochromatic light in optical pyrometers — ‘a factor of fundamental importance’.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess if instrument articles explain the theory that justifies design choices and their limits (e.g., Wien’s law assumptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of technological progression and likely replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment that the ‘disappearing filament’ pyrometer has been greatly developed and ‘in time, it will supplant most of the other types now in use for high-temperature measurements.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good reviews note emerging technologies and plausibly evaluate their potential to replace older methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhythm of work as determinant of efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Every one is well aware that once a rhythm, or the proper co-ordination in the play of a set of muscles in the performance of some definite act, is mastered, not only is the energy expenditure reduced ... but there is an actual enhancement of the ease with which we perform the specified act.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In studies of manual work, measure/describe preferred rhythms and their effect on energy expenditure and efficiency; consider habit and training effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rest characteristics (duration, type, posture-change) relative to work
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Rest is best obtained, not by simple quiescence, but by change of posture; slow movement of another type ... will ... give the most beneficial results.’ Also notes little attention to duration of rest periods in relation to work done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should assess optimal rest scheduling and active-rest modalities rather than simple inactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nutrition and undernutrition effects on performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient intake or poor food is ‘one of the chief sources of general inefficiency’; chronic undernutrition lowers efficiency and increases disease susceptibility; wartime evidence indicates large reductions in working capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating human performance, include nutritional status as a major explanatory variable and report experimental evidence where available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Psychic factors and monotony in work efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The response of the organism to the multiple psychic imponderabilia ... Man is, in the main, a psychic chameleon.’ Monotony interacts with fatigue and temperament determines the perception of monotony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include psychological/environmental factors (monotony, temperament, attention) when explaining variability in worker efficiency; beware of treating output as solely physiological.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental and equipment factors affecting output
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors such as lighting, heating, ventilation, seating, machine design, and workplace temperature/humidity strongly influence output; examples cited show output varies with temperature and lighting (electric vs daylight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report how environmental conditions and ergonomic design influence productivity; include quantitative observations when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for cooperation between scientists, employers and employees
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The quest of efficiency calls for the closest and most intimate co-operation between the scientific investigator, the employer, and the employee ...’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend collaborative approaches for implementing efficiency improvements and for designing practical, acceptable interventions in industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational/experimental technique and data-quality considerations in eclipse/astronomical tests
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Einstein eclipse test: factors that add weight are observers pointing directly on the stars (avoiding use of a ceelostat or other mirror); photographing another star-field during totality to obtain an independent scale-value; camera definition and star-field brightness affect measurement reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate observational results by examining instrumentation choices (direct pointing vs mirrors), independent scale calibration strategies, camera resolution/definition, and the brightness/quality of star fields; recognise that plate scale and instrument quality heavily influence the confidence of derived physical conclusions.
